_comment: Known-divergence baseline for rust/tools/oracle-conformance.ps1's hc-conformance.exe self-check gate. A ratchet, not a target (see CLAUDE.md 'Build the differential measurement before the change'): a fixture id listed here is tolerated when hc-conformance.exe reports it FAIL; any FAIL not listed here is a NEW divergence and fails the gate. Remove an entry once a fixture is fixed/reconciled -- never add one without recording why below. machine_commit is the submodule pin PanGloss's own machine submodule carries (branch integrate-conformance-framework), chosen as oracle of record because the exe used to measure this baseline was built from that exact commit (verified: exe LastWriteTime postdates the commit's own commit time) in two independent worktrees (the main checkout and .worktrees/pin-<commit>), both producing byte-identical PASS/FAIL outcomes over every fixture in this file.

divergences.note: SIGNATURE matches the founding oracle exactly for both of dakimo's two analyses. The rules: field cannot be verified by hc-conformance.exe's self-check for a structural reason: both declared parses render to the IDENTICAL signature "DAK+IMO|dakimo", and the self-check's per-signature rule-attribution check (Runner.cs) compares EVERY declared parse against EVERY actual result sharing that signature -- for two derivations with genuinely different rule sets under one shared signature, this always reports exactly one mismatch per declared entry, regardless of which of the two correct rule-set assignments is chosen (verified empirically: swapping the assignment only changes which mismatch is reported, not whether one is). words.yaml's rules: values instead follow this fixture's own documented semantics (crLeftHead ~ root_index 0 ~ DAK-headed; crRightHead ~ root_index 1 ~ IMO-headed), independently confirmed by cross_compiler_equivalence_gate.rs's RED-2 test.
